# Volume 1 — CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

For reasons she knew best herself, Thirza refrained from informing Nell about remaining at Grey Shutters until the subsequent afternoon. She occupied the child with different chores throughout the morning, observing her with a sharp gaze as she completed them. By midday, she had decided that Nell was intelligent and compliant, ready to labor and prompt to comprehend; her major fault appeared to be an inclination to drift into reveries halfway through a chore and lose track of it completely until she was abruptly brought back to reality by a scolding or a disaster.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0000 }

As soon as Nell was done with the dinner dishes, she abruptly faced Thirza, possessing the demeanor and look of somebody fiercely set on discovering the worst. Her slight, small frame shook all over; her cheeks reddened and her pupils widened to the point of turning nearly black; she squeezed her hands together firmly and stated with a beseeching tone:
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0001 }

“Oh, I beg you, Miss Abernethy, will you not inform me whether you intend to dismiss me or keep me? Throughout the entire morning I have striven to remain patient, yet I truly believe I am unable to endure this uncertainty a moment longer. The sensation is terrible. I implore you to tell me.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0002 }

“You failed to rinse the dishcloth with fresh boiling water like I instructed,” Thirza stated firmly. “Go handle that right now prior to asking additional questions, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0003 }

Nell departed to take care of the dishcloth, after which she came back to Thirza and fixed begging eyes upon the face of the latter.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0004 }

“Well,” stated Thirza, who could not discover any pretext to delay her clarification any further, “I guess I may as well inform you. Obed and I have resolved to retain you—provided, that is, you attempt to be a dutiful little girl and prove that you are appreciative. Why, child, what on earth is wrong?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0005 }

“Tears are falling from my eyes,” Nell remarked, sounding confused. “The reason escapes me. My joy couldn't be greater. Actually, glad fails to properly describe it. Feeling glad matched my experience with the cherry blossoms on Petal Road—whereas this! Ah, it goes far beyond mere gladness. Such happiness fills me. Trying to act as good as possible will be my goal. That promises to be a difficult struggle, considering how frequently Mrs. Thomas remarked on my extreme wickedness. Even so, my utmost efforts will be given. Still, are you able to explain my tears to me?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0006 }

“I guess it is due to your being so worked up and excited,” Thirza stated with disapproval. “Take a seat on that chair and attempt to compose yourself. Both crying and laughing come way too easily to you, I am afraid. Yes, your staying here is permitted, and our endeavor will be to do right by you. Attending school is a necessity for you; however, with vacation merely two weeks away, starting prior to its reopening in September is not worthwhile.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0007 }

“By what name should I address you?” inquired Nell. “Must I perpetually say Miss Abernethy? Is it permissible for me to call you Aunt Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0008 }

“No; you can just address me as Thirza. Being called Miss Abernethy is something I am unaccustomed to, and it would cause me to feel nervous.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0009 }

“To simply say Thirza feels terribly impolite,” Nell objected.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0010 }

“Provided you are mindful to address me with deference, I suppose doing so will not be rude. With the exception of the clergyman, every person in Brierley, regardless of age, refers to me as Thirza. On occasions when it occurs to him, he says Miss Abernethy.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0011 }

“It would give me great pleasure to address you as Aunt Thirza,” Nell uttered with longing. “There has never been an aunt or a single relative in my life—a grandmother included. Calling you that would create a sense that I truly was part of your family. Would it be possible for me to address you as Aunt Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0012 }

“No. I am not an aunt to you, and I disbelieve in using names for people that do not belong to them.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0013 }

“However, it was possible for us to pretend that you were an aunt to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0014 }

“It wasn’t possible for me,” Thirza stated with a grim expression.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0015 }

“Are things never imagined by you as being different than they actually exist?” Nell asked with wide eyes.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0016 }

“No.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0017 }

“Oh!” A deep breath was taken by Nell. “Oh, Miss—Thirza, how great is your loss!”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0018 }

“I refuse to hold with picturing things other than how they actually exist,” Thirza shot back. “If the Lord places us in particular situations, His intent is not for us to pretend they do not exist. Which brings something to mind. Step inside the sitting room, Nell—ensure your shoes are free of dirt and refrain from admitting flies—and fetch the picture card resting upon the mantelpiece. It features the Lord’s Prayer, and you will spend your free time later today memorizing every word. Such prayers as I listened to yesterday evening shall not happen again.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0019 }

“I guess I was quite clumsy,” Nell stated in an apologetic way, “however, you know, I had not ever practiced before. It isn't reasonable to anticipate that someone would pray expertly on her initial attempt, is it? Following my going to sleep, I devised a wonderful prayer, precisely as I gave you my word I would do. That prayer was almost the length of a clergyman's and immensely poetic. Yet can you imagine it? Not a single word remained in my memory upon my waking earlier today. Moreover, I am worried that I shall not manage to compose a replacement of such quality ever again. For some reason, ideas are not as fine once they are conceived again. Has that ever caught your attention?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0020 }

“Pay attention to this, Nell. Whenever I instruct you to perform a task, my expectation is that you carry it out immediately rather than remaining motionless and debating the matter. Simply depart and carry out my instructions.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0021 }

Nell immediately went over to the sitting-room on the other side of the hallway; when she did not come back; Thirza set her knitting aside after waiting ten minutes and strode after her with a stern look on her face. She discovered Nell standing without moving in front of a painting that hung on the wall in the space between the two windows, her eyes shining brightly with dreams. The white and green illumination filtering through the apple-trees and tangled vines outdoors washed over the enthralled small form with a nearly ethereal glow.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0022 }

“What on earth has come over you, Nell?” Thirza inquired with severity.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0023 }

With a jolt, Nell returned to reality.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0024 }

“That,” she stated, indicating the artwork—a fairly bright chromo called, “Christ Blessing Little Children”—“and I was simply picturing that I was a child in it—that I was the small girl wearing the blue dress, positioned apart by herself in the corner as though she belonged to no one, just like me. She appears lonely and unhappy, wouldn't you say? I suppose she didn't have a father or mother to call her own. Yet she desired to receive a blessing, too, so she merely sneaked timidly up to the edge of the gathering, trusting no one would pay attention to her—save Him. I am certain I understand precisely what she experienced. Her heart must have pounded and her hands must have turned cold, just as mine did when I inquired if I could remain. She feared He may not see her. However, He probably did, wouldn't you agree? I have been attempting to picture the whole scene—her moving slightly closer the entire time until she stood right beside Him; and after that He would glance at her and place His hand upon her hair and oh, what a rush of happiness would sweep through her! Still, I wish the painter had not depicted Him looking so mournful. Every picture of Him is that way, if you have observed. Even so, I do not think He could actually have appeared that unhappy, otherwise the children would have felt frightened of Him.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0025 }

“Nell,” Thirza said, questioning why she had failed to interrupt this talk much earlier, “you ought not to speak like that. It is disrespect—absolute disrespect.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0026 }

The eyes of Nell were filled with wonder.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0027 }

“Well, my feelings were as respectful as they could possibly be. It certainly was not my intention to show disrespect.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0028 }

“Well, I do not imagine that you did—nevertheless, discussing these matters so casually lacks propriety. Furthermore, Nell, whenever I dispatch you to fetch an item, you are required to deliver it immediately without slipping into daydreaming or lost thoughts in front of paintings. Keep that in mind. Pick up that card and proceed straight into the kitchen. At present, take a seat in the corner and memorize that prayer completely.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0029 }

Nell positioned the card to rest upon the pitcher of apple blossoms that she had carried inside for the embellishment of the dinner table—a piece of decor Thirza had viewed with suspicion, though she had remained quiet—rested her chin atop her hands, and proceeded to examine it with deep concentration over a few quiet minutes.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0030 }

“I like this,” she declared after some time. “It’s lovely. I’ve heard it previously—I heard the asylum Sunday-school superintendent recite it one time. But I didn’t like it on that occasion. He possessed a voice that was so cracked and he prayed it in such a mournful manner. I truly felt certain he believed praying was an unpleasant obligation. This is not poetry, yet it causes me to feel the exact same way poetry does. ‘Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name.’ That resembles a line of music. Oh, I’m so happy you considered having me memorize this, Miss—Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0031 }

“Indeed, master it and keep quiet,” Thirza snapped.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0032 }

Nell tilted the vessel holding the apple blossoms close enough that she could plant a gentle kiss upon a pink-cupped bud, after which she spent several additional moments studying with great diligence.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0033 }

“Thirza,” she asked a moment later, “do you believe that a intimate friend will ever be mine in Brierley?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0034 }

“A—a friend of what nature?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0035 }

“A close companion—a true confidant, as you understand—a genuinely like-minded soul to whom I may reveal my deepest thoughts. I have envisioned encountering her my entire existence. I did not actually imagine I ever would, yet a great number of my sweetest fantasies have materialized simultaneously, so it may be that this dream realizes itself as well. Is it your opinion that this could happen?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0036 }

“Isolde Pembroke’s house is over at Pear Hill, and her age is close to yours. A very nice little girl, she might become a playmate for you upon her return home. At present, she is visiting her aunt over at Delford. However, you must mind your behavior carefully. A very particular woman, Mrs. Pembroke will not permit Isolde to play with a little girl unless she is nice and good.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0037 }

Thirza was observed through the apple blossoms by Nell, whose eyes shone with interest.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0038 }

“How does Isolde look? She doesn’t have red hair, does she? Oh, I really hope she doesn't. Having red hair myself is terrible enough, but I absolutely could not tolerate it in a close friend.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0039 }

“Isolde is an extremely lovely young girl. Her cheeks are rosy, and her hair and eyes are black. Furthermore, she possesses goodness and intelligence, traits that surpass mere beauty.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0040 }

Thirza had a penchant for morals that matched the Duchess's in Wonderland, believing steadfastly that each statement addressed to a child in the process of being raised ought to have one attached.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0041 }

However, Nell carelessly dismissed the lesson and grabbed solely onto the charming prospects that lay ahead of it.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0042 }

“Oh, I am deeply relieved that she possesses beauty. Short of being gorgeous oneself—an impossibility for me—possessing a gorgeous closest friend would be the finest thing. During my stay at Mrs. Thomas’s home, a glass-doored bookcase stood in her parlor. Books were entirely absent from inside it; Mrs. Thomas used the space for storing her finest chinaware and her jams—whenever she possessed any jams to store. A single door had been shattered. Mr. Thomas broke it one evening while he was somewhat drunk. The opposite door remained intact, however, and I made believe that the image of myself reflected there was a different young girl residing inside it. I named her Lettie Marchant, and our bond was exceptionally close. Hours were spent conversing with her, particularly on Sundays, as I shared every detail with her. Lettie proved to be the solace and relief of my existence. Our game was to feign that the bookcase possessed magic, and provided I merely discovered the charm, I might unlock the glass and walk directly into the space where Lettie Marchant resided, rather than into the china and jam shelves belonging to Mrs. Thomas. Subsequently, Lettie Marchant would have clasped my hand, guiding me outside toward an extraordinary realm filled entirely with blossoms, light, and magical beings, where we would reside in bliss perpetually. Upon moving to the home of Mrs. Rudge, parting from Lettie Marchant utterly shattered my spirit. She experienced the sorrow intensely as well, I am certain of it, because tears fell as her lips pressed against mine through the glass of the bookcase to bid me farewell. Mrs. Rudge’s place lacked a bookcase. Nevertheless, a short distance up the stream from the residence lay a narrow, verdant small glen, which housed the most exquisite reverberation. That spot repeated every spoken word, even when spoken without any loudness at all. Consequently, I pictured that the sound was a young girl named Melisande, leading us to become wonderful companions, and my affection for her nearly equaled my love for Lettie Marchant—not entirely equal, but very close, as you realize. On the evening prior to my departure for the asylum, I bade farewell to Melisande, and oh, her parting words returned to me carrying such mournful, mournful inflections. My devotion to her had grown so strong that I lacked the spirit to picture a closest companion at the asylum, even supposing any room for fantasy existed in that place.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0043 }

“It is probably best that none existed,” Thirza remarked tartly. “Such antics do not meet with my approval. You appear to partially credit your own daydreams. Having a genuine, living companion to dispel these foolish thoughts from your mind will do you good. However, avoid speaking of your Lettie Marchants and your Violettas within earshot of Mrs. Pembroke, lest she conclude that you fabricate tales.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0044 }

“Oh, I will not. I was unable to speak of them to just anyone—they possess memories far too sacred for such a thing. However, I believed I would enjoy letting you learn about them. Oh, see, a large bee has just fallen right out of an apple blossom. Imagine what a delightful location for a home—inside an apple blossom! Picture falling asleep within it while it was being rocked by the wind. Were I not a human girl, I believe I would prefer being a bee and dwelling within the blossoms.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0045 }

“You wished to be a sea-gull yesterday,” Thirza sniffed. “It appears to me that you are extremely fickle minded. My instructions were for you to study that prayer instead of talking. Yet you seem incapable of ceasing your chatter whenever someone is willing to hear you. Therefore, head to your room and commit it to memory.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0046 }

“Oh, I have almost the entire thing memorized at this point—everything except the final line.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0047 }

“Oh well, it does not matter, follow my instructions. Return to your bedchamber and complete memorizing it thoroughly, remaining there until I summon you below to assist me with preparing tea.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0048 }

“May I bring the apple blossoms along to keep me company?” begged Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0049 }

“No; you have no desire for your room to be filled with flowers. In the beginning, you ought to have left them on the tree.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0050 }

“I also experienced a slight feeling of that nature,” Nell remarked. “In a way, I believed I ought not to curtail their beautiful existence through picking them—were I an apple blossom, I would not wish to be plucked. However, the urge could not be resisted. How do you handle encountering a temptation that is irresistible?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0051 }

“Nell, were you listening when I told you to go to your room?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0052 }

Nell uttered a sigh, withdrew to the eastern gable, and took a seat upon a chair beside the window.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0053 }

“There—that prayer is familiar to me. That final sentence was learned by me while ascending the stairs. Now I shall picture objects into this room in order that they will remain imagined forever. A white velvet carpet covered all over with pink roses coats the floor and pink silk curtains hang at the windows. Gold and silver brocade tapestry hangs on the walls. Mahogany comprises the furniture. Mahogany was never seen by me, yet the word sounds extremely opulent. Here is a couch entirely piled with magnificent silken cushions, pink, blue, crimson, and gold, and I am reclining on it with grace. My image is visible to me in that magnificent large mirror that hangs on the wall. Tall and regal, I am dressed in a sweeping white lace gown, bearing a pearl cross upon my breast and pearls within my hair. Midnight darkness describes my hair and a clear ivory pallor describes my skin. The Lady Lucinda Fitzgerald is my name. No, it is not—I am unable to cause that to feel genuine.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0054 }

Stepping briskly toward the small mirror, she took a look inside. Reflected in the glass was her own sharp, freckle-dusted face alongside her earnest grey eyes.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0055 }

“You are merely Nell of Grey Shutters,” she stated with deep sincerity, “and my mind pictures you, precisely as you appear at this moment, every time I endeavor to pretend that I am the Lady Lucinda. Nevertheless, being Nell of Grey Shutters is a million times sweeter than being Nell of no place at all, is it not?”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0056 }

Leaning down, she gave her mirror image a tender kiss, then made her way over to the open window.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0057 }

“Good afternoon, dear Frost Maiden. Likewise, good afternoon to the dear birches situated down in the hollow. Also, good afternoon to the dear gray house located up on the hill. I question whether Isolde will become my bosom friend. I trust that she becomes one, and I am going to love her deeply. Nevertheless, I ought to never fully forget Lettie Marchant and Melisande. If I were to do so, their feelings would be deeply wounded, and hurting anyone's feelings—even those of a little bookcase girl or a little echo girl—is something I would despise doing. I have to make sure to keep them in mind and dispatch a kiss to them each day.”
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0058 }

Nell sent two light kisses from the tips of her fingers beyond the cherry blossoms, after which she rested her chin on her hands and floated indulgently into a realm of fantasy.
{: #nw-v01-c08-p0059 }
